messages:
Maya: 🚨 heads up — canary deploy v2.14 started ~10m ago and we're seeing a sharp spike in 5xx rates for the inference API. Noticed around 1771002320 via synthetic checks. Paging now.

incident-bot: ALERT: prod.inference.5xx_rate > 3% for 5m (canary pool) — severity: high — paged: eng-oncall

Kunal: on it. which metric name are we looking at? is this a backend or model error?

Devon: I pushed the canary. We removed the old batching fallback and enabled new kv-cache eviction. I also added a new counter `model_inference_errors_total` in the release but didn't touch dashboards/alerts for it.

Maya: symptoms: higher p95 latency and 5xx spikes. A subset of hosted customers saw increased error rates ~2-3x. No obvious change in request volume.

Kunal: can you dump some logs for the failed requests? sample ids?

Maya: pasting sample stack traces and a short log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:08Z] request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=502 err="kv cache miss -> UnhandledException: kv-evict failed"
[2026-03-15T09:12:09Z] request_id=def456 route=/v1/generate status=504 err="Timed out waiting for model response"
```

Devon: hmm those look like the eviction path. I changed the eviction to sync mode to avoid stale cache but didn't add a retry/guard. Could cause transient failures under load.

Jen: customer-impact? any support tickets yet?

Maya: a few inbound chats about timeouts, one high-usage customer reported degraded throughput. Not full outage but SLO burn for the last 10m.

Kunal: two observability issues here: (1) the new counter `model_inference_errors_total` isn't on the infra dashboard, and (2) the alert rules still target `inference_5xx_rate` but it's aggregated differently now since we split canary pools, so thresholds are wrong -> noisy fires.

ops-bot: Runbook suggested: attempt feature-flag kill-switch for v2.14 canary or rollback. Recommend kill-switch first to reduce blast radius.

Devon: agreed. Flipping canary flag now: `rdwctl feature-flags set inference_v2_canary false --env=prod --actor=devon`

Maya: confirmed toggled. Traffic stopping to canary. Observed 30s after flag flip the 5xx rate is trending down.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic pager suppressed for alerts tied to canary pool (policy: 1m cooloff). Manual ack by Maya.

Kunal: good mitigation. We still need a rollback plan for the full rollout and an RCA for missing alert/dashboard wiring.

Devon: preparing a safe rollback/undo for the charted change. For k8s rollout: 

```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=152
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/inference-service
```

I'll hold the full rollback until we confirm no further customer impact — prefer to keep change isolated via flag for now.

Maya: FYI the alert rule that fired is this (copied from alert manager):

```
alert: High5xxRate
expr: sum(rate(inference_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(inference_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.03
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
```

Kunal: problem is the `pool` label changed to `deployment_pool` in the new metrics, so the grouping didn't match and we got mismatched aggregation. Also threshold was set on a global aggregation; when the canary was small the percent looked big.

Jen: action items for post-incident:
- patch dashboards to include `model_inference_errors_total` and `latency_p95_per_model` (Devon)
- update alert rules to use `deployment_pool` and add a customer-impacting alert for error-rate at product-level (Kunal)
- run a canary test harness to simulate kv-evict path (SRE + Dev)
- update runbook to include feature-flag kill-switch steps and `rdwctl` examples (Maya)

Devon: I'll own wiring the metric into dashboards and add a quick temporary alert mapping. Also will add a guard/retry around kv-evict in the next patch.

Maya: handing off to Kunal for overnight follow-up and RCA doc. I'm going offline in 20.

Kunal: taking handoff — I'll create an incident ticket, tag eng-release and product, and schedule a follow-up post-mortem. Initial notes:
- root cause: kv-cache eviction sync mode + missing retry -> intermittent UnhandledException
- observability gaps: new metric not surfaced, alert label rename mismatch, noisy firing rules obscured severity
- mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch applied, canary traffic cut, monitor for regressions

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-77 — paged teams: eng-release, eng-sre, product.

Maya: thanks all. leave whatever logs/queries you need in the ticket. Marking thread closed for now, will reopen if we see regression. :white_check_mark:

Devon: noted — will attach dashboard diffs and the small config patch to the ticket.

Kunal: will follow up with an action plan and estimated ETA for the alert/dashboard fixes in the morning.
